subject.title: after_tool_call hook receives a flattened string, not the structured ToolResult — plugins cannot detect exec/bash failures

question: Should OpenClaw canonicalize Codex-native shell/apply_patch after_tool_call payloads from app-server completion data instead of forwarding Codex's raw string PostToolUse tool_response as the plugin-visible result?
rationale: The bug is clear from source, but the repair changes the public plugin hook payload/timing boundary and must choose between native-relay immediacy, app-server structured fidelity, duplicate-event avoidance, and compatibility for text-only consumers.

options.title: Canonical structured OpenClaw payload
options.body: Use app-server commandExecution/fileChange completion data as the plugin-visible after_tool_call result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the raw string relay for those tools.

options.title: Wait for upstream Codex structure
options.body: Keep OpenClaw relay behavior stable and require Codex to emit structured shell/exec PostToolUse payloads before OpenClaw changes the plugin event.

options.title: Document raw string as contract
options.body: Treat Codex native PostToolUse strings as intended and direct plugins needing exit codes to a different surface, accepting the reported observability gap.

recommendation.title: Canonical structured OpenClaw payload
recommendation.body: Use app-server commandExecution/fileChange completion data as the plugin-visible after_tool_call result for Codex-native shell/apply_patch and suppress the raw string relay for those tools.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision affects the public plugin tool-result boundary introduced and scoped in the harness middleware work.
